<!-- This template is for Devs to give QA details before moving the issue To-Test -->
### Summary
This resolves an issue that was preventing the detail page from rendering. #12237 introduced a change that would prevent errors from being thrown if `fetch()` was invoked against a route without any keys in its query - a use case that was required for navigating between tabs in edit views.

This fix attempts to address a change in timing between route watchers and component unmounting by slightly modifying the approach taken in #12237 by watching the route and only allowing `fetch()` to re-invoke if the route hasn't changed. The differences observed appear to be related to:

- Vue2: Component unmounts before the route watcher invokes
- Vue3: Watcher triggers before the component unmounts, potentially raising unhandled exceptions during navigation between pages & tabs 

Fixes #12267 
Fixes #12275
<!-- Define findings related to the feature or bug issue. -->

### Occurred changes and/or fixed issues
<!-- Include information of the changes, including collateral areas which have been affected by this PR as requirement or for convenience. -->

- watch `$route` instead of `$route.query` in ResourceDetail
- assert that `$route.name` hasn't changed before invoking `fetch()` 

### Areas or cases that should be tested
<!-- Areas that should be tested can include Airgap checks, Rancher upgrades, K8s upgrade, etc. -->
<!-- Which browser did you use for local testing? The reviewer should test with a different browser. -->
<!-- Add missing steps or rewrite them if have been missed or to complement existing information. This should define a clear way to reproduce it and not an approximation. -->

This modifies `fetch()` behavior for all edit components. Navigation between edit pages and tabs needs to be tested.

### Areas which could experience regressions
<!-- Create a detailed list of areas to be analyzed which may be affected by the changes, which would require a prior research to avoid regressions. -->

Navigation and data fetching for edit components.

author: ianw
body:
## Changes
 
Currently the man pages in the generated doc site don't link to each other.  A
standard link: approach doesn't work that well when the target is both a groff
man page and the HTML site, as you don't want the links in the man page.
    
This is something other projects have faced, git in particular uses adoc for
man pages and the approach here is styled on its "gitlink:" macro.  The .js
version is for Antora which uses the asciidoctorjs internally and there is an
asciidoc plugin for the man page generation.  The ruby version is included just
in case we want to geneate man pages from asciidoctor directly one day.
    
For the HTML output it is a link to the page (or, can be marked for external
looukup for other tools).  For the man pages, it's just a usual "strong" text.
    
I've been through the existing references to convert them to the new macro.

author: cooljeanius
body:
Fixes [https://github.com/cooljeanius/bnetd/security/code-scanning/3](https://github.com/cooljeanius/bnetd/security/code-scanning/3)

To fix the use-after-free issue, we need to ensure that the pointer `q` is not accessed after it has been freed. The best way to achieve this is to add a `continue` statement after freeing `q` to skip the rest of the loop iteration. This will prevent any further use of `q` in that iteration.

- Modify the code in the function `mailbox_get_list` to add a `continue` statement after freeing `q` when the memory allocation for `sender` fails.
- This change should be made in the file `bnetd/bnetd-0.4.27.2/src/bnetd/mail.c` around line 408.

author: gonzalad
body:
Hello, this PR should make it easier to use the library with a corporate maven repository.

The PR addresses:
* https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator-cli/issues/835).
* https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator-cli/issues/652

@wing328 or @kay-schecker is it possible for you to review this PR please ?

Contents of this PR:

1. fix NO_PROXY issue  
    This is done by removing explicit handling of HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY: Axios already handles that (see https://github.com/axios/axios#request-config). 
1. added `generator-cli.http.rejectUnauthorized` configuration to avoid the error `unable to get local issuer certificate`.
1. support using placeholders for environment variables in any configuration value.
   this will allow to use env vars to set credentials in the queryUrl or downloadUrl: 
   Usage:  
	```
	{
	  "$schema": "./node_modules/@openapitools/openapi-generator-cli/config.schema.json",
	  "spaces": 2,
	  "generator-cli": {
	    "version": "7.9.0",
	    "repository": {
	      "downloadUrl": "https://${MVN_USERNAME}:${MVN_PASSWORD}@mynexus.com/repository/maven-proxy-group/${groupId}/${artifactId}/${versionName}/${artifactId}-${versionName}.jar"
	    }
	  }
	}

	``` 
1. For people using a nexus registry for both npm and maven registry: add support for retrieving authToken in .npmrc and using the npm token to authenticate to the maven repository.  
   * the credentials for connecting to maven repository (authToken) are retrieved from .npmrc file
   (the credentials used is the one matching the url of the maven server).
   * also, if strict-ssl is set to false in npmrc, then certificate verification is disabled
   Usage:  
	```
	{
	  "$schema": "./node_modules/@openapitools/openapi-generator-cli/config.schema.json",
	  "spaces": 2,
	  "generator-cli": {
	    "version": "7.9.0",
	    "repository": {
	      "downloadUrl": "https://mynexus.com/repository/maven-proxy-group/${groupId}/${artifactId}/${versionName}/${artifactId}-${versionName}.jar"
	    },
	    "useNpmrc": true
	  }
	}
	``` 
1. Fix for running unit tests on windows
1. Activates logging (I had some issues testing the library on a project, and the library didn't output any logs)

Thanks for making this! I'm getting familiar with depth maps, and would like to add this feature to [Lume 3D HTML elements](https://lume.io).

This PR removes Parcel, making `npm install` a lot quicker, and the app running as a plain vanilla static web app.

This is nice because the code works on the standards (added `.js` extension in the `import`, added the `importmap`, and replaced the non-standard import of the image with a standard path relative to `import.meta.url` which modern bundlers understand), and then anyone else can optimize it with any tool they want however they want, while the possibility of the app breaking is removed from maintenance of the repo.

I also included `package-lock.json` which means that running `npm clean-install` instead of `npm install` will guarantee that the exact versions of any dependencies will be installed as when the lock file was created and tested (whereas `npm install` will update libraries to in-range compatible versions, which sometimes can break things).

author: andrewhess
body:
# Description
This attaches the new query pipeline for API queries. However, the old pipeline is still used instead of the new pipeline. This PR also has several bug fixes found when trying to run simple queries (see the commit titles for info about which bugs were fixed)

To use the new pipeline, in config.go you have to make this return `true`:
```
func IsNewQueryPipelineEnabled() bool {
	return false
}
```

When the new pipeline is enabled, some simple queries work. For example `*` and `city=Boston` seem to work when using API queries like this:
```
curl -X POST -d '{
    "searchText": "city=Boston",
    "indexName": "*",
    "startEpoch": "now-24h",
    "endEpoch": "now",
    "queryLanguage": "Splunk QL"
}' http://localhost:5122/api/search | python3 -m json.tool | less
```

**Limitation:** no SPL commands are implemented for the new query pipeline, so piping the search into anything else like `stats` or `eval` will not work

## Known Issues
1. When there's no data ingested, running a query gives an error instead of no results
2. There's an issue getting unrotated data
3. When multiple segments are ingested and PQS is enabled, there's several errors logged indicating the block tracker is nil, so it searches all blocks. The result returned to the client appears to be correct though


# Testing
1. Enabled the new pipeline
2. Ingested two segments of data
3. Ran `*` and `city=Boston` queries

author: susumutomita
body:
Update the Dashboard component to include a rich UI for displaying field availability.

* Add import statements for various UI components from "@/components/ui".
* Define the `FieldAvailability` interface to structure the data.
* Add state variables `data`, `selectedDate`, and `selectedField` to manage the dashboard state.
* Implement the `fetchData` function to fetch data from the `/api/data` endpoint and update the `data` state.
* Use the `useEffect` hook to call `fetchData` when `selectedDate` or `selectedField` changes.
* Extract unique field names from the `data` state using the `uniqueFields` constant.
* Add UI components including `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardContent`, `Calendar`, `Select`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`, `Table`, `TableHeader`, `TableRow`, `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableCell`, and `Button` to render the dashboard.
* Display the field availability in a table format with date, time, field, and availability status.
* Add a button to manually fetch and update the data.

---

For more details, open the [Copilot Workspace session](https://copilot-workspace.githubnext.com/susumutomita/ground-reservation-frontend?shareId=96bb3e23-ce83-4c5b-b59a-0a182ac23e84).

body:
This pull request introduces new functionality to manage liked songs in the Spotify plugin. The most important changes include adding commands to like, remove, and toggle the like status of the currently playing track, and updating the Spotify client to support these operations.

### New Commands and Features:

* [`SpotifyPlugin.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-1bfa7aba7b2a230357136cb37f9396c44e62b66ea3fa23d309de69582ad79faaR68-R70): Added new commands `like`, `remove`, and `toggle` to manage the like status of the currently playing track. 

* [`SpotifyPlugin.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-1bfa7aba7b2a230357136cb37f9396c44e62b66ea3fa23d309de69582ad79faaR343-R365): Implemented methods `AddLikeCurrentSong`, `RemoveLikeCurrentSong`, and `ToggleLikeCurrentSong` to handle the new commands.

### Spotify Client Enhancements:

* [`SpotifyPluginClient.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-0ed9103ee97c67b8d468950d9a4ab6151af1a08c0467d58575fa01d6dfc6420dR92-R108): Added `CurrentPlaybackId` property to retrieve the ID of the currently playing track or episode. 

* [`SpotifyPluginClient.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-0ed9103ee97c67b8d468950d9a4ab6151af1a08c0467d58575fa01d6dfc6420dR275-R320): Implemented methods `CheckLikedById`, `ToggleLikeById`, `LikeById`, `RemoveLikeById`, `AddLikeCurrentSong`, `RemoveLikeCurrentSong`, and `ToggleLikeCurrentSong` to support the new commands.

* [`SpotifyPluginClient.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-0ed9103ee97c67b8d468950d9a4ab6151af1a08c0467d58575fa01d6dfc6420dR382-R390): Updated `ConnectWebClient` to include `UserLibraryModify` scope for modifying liked songs. 

### Documentation Updates:

* [`README.md`](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R32-R34): Updated the command list to include `sp like`, `sp remove`, and `sp toggle` for managing liked songs.

* [`SpotifyPlugin.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-1bfa7aba7b2a230357136cb37f9396c44e62b66ea3fa23d309de69582ad79faaR68): Introduced the `like` command and implemented the `LikeCurrentSong` method to handle the liking of the current song.

<!--
* Contributors are encouraged to read our [CONTRIBUTING](/CONTRIBUTING.md) documentation.
* Both Contributor and Reviewer Checklists are available at https://datadoghq.dev/datadog-agent/guidelines/contributing/#pull-requests.
* The pull request:
  * Should only fix one issue or add one feature at a time.
  * Must update the test suite for the relevant functionality.
  * Should pass all status checks before being reviewed or merged.
* Commit titles should be prefixed with general area of pull request's change.
* Please fill the below sections if possible with relevant information or links.
-->
### What does this PR do?

While working with a colleague on another task, I noticed that fetching secrets took a surprisingly long time. Moving secrets fetching and our JUnit XML upload operations to a separate step helps clean up the signal we get from Pipeline Visibility regarding Regression Detector job execution times.

### Motivation

More meaningful statistics from SMP's Test Visibility monitoring.

### Describe how to test/QA your changes

SMP tests should continue to be uploaded to Test Visibility.

### Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs

We use Pipeline Visibility to get a quick aggregate view of SMP's health in Agent CI -- particularly to understand if Agent CI jobs are terminating due to timeouts. If secrets fetching or uploading JUnit XML take nontrivial amounts of time (say, more than a dozen seconds each), then we mistakenly attribute GitLab CI timeouts to under-provisioning of SMP runners in our backend, potentially causing us to overallocate capacity. Moving the JUnit XML upload step to a separate job should fix that attribution problem.

author: htunnicliff
body:
I added a tip explaining how to use the `TERM_PROGRAM` environment variable to conditionally use shim-based activation. 

---

For background, I use zsh and have my `.zprofile` configured to activate mise like so:

```zsh
eval "$($HOME/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"
```

However, as these docs already mention, IDEs such as VSCode don't always function as expected unless mise is activated with `--shims`.

To get the best of both worlds, mise activation can be conditionally modified if terminal detection is used, which is what I added to the docs:

```zsh
# ~/.zprofile
if [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" == "vscode" ]]; then
  eval "$($HOME/.local/bin/mise activate zsh --shims)"
elif; then
  eval "$($HOME/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"
fi
```

>   - Implement methods for fetching and managing campaigns
>   - Use the Google Ads API client library
>

>   - Add method for creating and scheduling posts
> 
> - Update `app/Services/LinkedInAdsService.php`
>   - Add method for c...

**Continue chatting at https://sweep-chat-demo.vercel.app/c/473935e5-77d3-49cd-a7f0-c75d0588cc25.**

# Purpose
This pull request adds the ability to schedule and publish social media posts to various platforms, including Facebook, LinkedIn, and others. This feature will allow users to plan and manage their social media content more effectively.

# Description
The changes in this pull request include:

1. **AdvertisingAccountResource**: Added new fields to the `AdvertisingAccountResource` form to support Google Ads integration, including `developer_token`, `client_id`, and `client_secret`.
2. **SocialMediaPostResource**: Added new fields to the `SocialMediaPostResource` form to support scheduling and publishing of social media posts, including `scheduled_at`, `platforms`, `link`, and `image`. Also added a new "Publish" action to the resource that allows users to publish scheduled posts to the configured platforms.
3. **FacebookAdsService**: Implemented a new `createAndSchedulePost` method to create and schedule Facebook posts using the Facebook Ads API.
4. **GoogleAdsService**: Implemented new methods to create, update, and delete Google Ads campaigns using the Google Ads API.
5. **LinkedInAdsService**: Implemented a new `createAndSchedulePost` method to create and schedule LinkedIn posts using the LinkedIn Ads API.

# Summary
The key changes in this pull request include:

- `app/Filament/App/Resources/AdvertisingAccountResource.php`: Added new fields to support Google Ads integration.
- `app/Filament/App/Resources/SocialMediaPostResource.php`: Added new fields and a "Publish" action to support scheduling and publishing of social media posts.
- `app/Services/FacebookAdsService.php`: Implemented a new method to create and schedule Facebook posts.
- `app/Services/GoogleAdsService.php`: Implemented new methods to manage Google Ads campaigns.
- `app/Services/LinkedInAdsService.php`: Implemented a new method to create and schedule LinkedIn posts.
- `config/services.php`: Added new configuration for Google Ads API credentials.
